Measured across 14 requests: no 401, 403, or 429 occurred. The server accepted a request supplying only limit=1, so player, tract_id, region_number, offset, and orderBy are not required for acceptance; limit is intentionally unmeasured because its requiredness was not tested in isolation and its omission is entangled with unexplained silence. Not required for acceptance does not establish that omission has no effect on scope: every returned row carried tract_id=1 and region_number=1, so an omitted selector may be silently defaulted rather than genuinely unscoped. Paging probes recorded for this route were offset=0, offset=5, limit=10000, three calls omitting all parameters, and orderBy=desc: offset=0 returned zero rows; offset=5 returned the first four rows of the omitted-offset response; limit=10000 returned 10000 rows (32.9 MB); the three omitted-parameter calls returned zero bytes; and orderBy=desc returned an empty data array. Limit was honored at 10000; whether a higher value behaves likewise was not measured. Whether omission changes scope remains unmeasured. No default response contract is declared because the two unparameterized attempts timed out without an HTTP response; only the captured limit and orderBy variants have contracts.

Measured live 2026-09-07 from this repository against three deeds. The response is {status, data} with data an object holding a cards array and an items array. A deed with nothing staked returns both arrays present and empty and data present and non-null, so the shared empty-result short-circuit does not apply to this route and the declarative fingerprint alone would reject that body: the 51 paths below data.cards[] and data.items[] cannot be observed in an empty collection. The contract therefore keeps the specification-derived 55-path fingerprint, which two populated bodies matched exactly with no type contradiction, and validates through the registered predicate land.stake.deeds-assets, which enforces the same declarations per row and accepts an empty collection. requiredKeyPaths is retained as a description of the body and is not enforced while a predicate is registered. The predicate tolerates a null in any declared field because only thirteen rows from two deeds have been observed and no deed carrying a staked Runi was among them; that tolerance records the absence of evidence and is not a statement that any field is nullable. Three keys present in every observed row are not declared, because each was null in every observation and a null-only observation establishes no type: data.cards[].delegated_to, data.cards[].rental_type and data.items[].stake_ref_id. They are returned to the caller unchanged. The boost, production-point and work figures on this route are JSON strings; the sibling deed-details route returns the deed-level equivalents as JSON numbers, and neither contract normalises toward the other. See library/observations/land-stake-2026-09-07.md.

Measured live 2026-09-07 from this repository. The response is {status, data}, and data changes JSON type within this one route: an object carrying uid, dec_stake_needed, dec_staked and dec_stake_in_use when the upstream has a record, and an empty array when either declared-required parameter is missing. One declarative contract covers both, because the shared empty-result definition recognises an empty data array and the contract matcher short-circuits on it before comparing types; no request variant is declared, because a variant is chosen by the caller at bind time and cannot express a branch the response chooses. Neither declared-required query parameter is enforced: a call omitting region_uid and a call with no parameters at all both answered HTTP 200 with an empty array, so both are recorded as measuredRequired false and the registered tool refuses a request that does not carry both. A valid region with no stake for the account returned a full object of zero figures rather than an empty array. Classification 2026-09-08: this public route fabricates content rather than being gated, broken or redundant. Only the exact casing GRAIN produced a real DEC-GRAIN entry; lowercase grain produced only a synthesised VESTING-grain entry, and VOUCHER and SPS produced only synthesised null-balance entries. Pool ids 1, 34 and 67 returned different quotes for the same amount. Zero and negative amounts clamped to 0/0, non-numeric amounts returned HTTP 400, and an unknown well-formed pool returned 0/0. Measured collection evidence: GET /cards/collection/{username} is public, has exactly the {player,cards[]} envelope at every measured size, has no upstream pagination or narrower query, and ranged from 376 cards / 0.46 MiB to 125,086 cards / 162,486,671 uncompressed bytes / 155 MiB across eight measured accounts. The detailed size and memory record is `library/observations/collection-streaming-memory-2026-09-08.md`. The listed query parameters are server-local filters and cursor controls; they are marked inert upstream because the upstream request receives only the username path. This entry records client-side pagination because the upstream provides no pagination. The server's collection tool streams cards[], projects ten core identity-and-value fields plus the optional decimal-string land_base_pp, counts matching cards, and retains only the requested page (at most 100 cards) in one 60-second page-cache slot per username; a different cursor or filter re-streams and re-parses the full collection and replaces that slot, and the cached page is re-streamed after expiry. It never raises the global 2 MiB response cap. The selected 90-second route timeout is the server's choice with the measured 41-second fetch behind it, and this route makes one timeout attempt rather than retrying it. Fixture tests use a deliberately small trimmed response and do not represent the 155 MiB sample. The server remains version 0.0.0 with no remote delivery path. The min_land_base_pp parameter is implemented locally, never sent upstream, and does not assert measured upstream support or non-support. Missing power is unknown and cannot match the minimum filter. Card definitions are joined locally by numeric card_detail_id from the full /cards/get_details response, cached as a projected map for 24 hours. Color matches primary or secondary wire color and subtype matches sub_type, both case-insensitive exact. These fields are local filters, not upstream query claims. At most two distinct GETs are allowed for this tool. Metadata failure stops before collection streaming. Separate definition provenance and a full-stream missing-definition count accompany each page. Local staked=yes/no/plot and numeric stake_plot_id filter capture-time staking_status; no excludes cooling, pending and unknown states. Plot mode requires the numeric selector and it is rejected in other modes. Optional stake_start_date/stake_end_date (timestamp or null) and stake_plot (positive integer or null) are strictly projected if present. Public client predicates provide semantic evidence; the retained live collection fixture omits these fields, so live wire verification and padded plot labels remain outstanding. InertUpstream here denotes never forwarded, not a probe result. Normalized element/secondary_element derive from the official client wire-color mapping; local element matches either. The selected metadata level supplies land_abilities; missing level entries are explicitly unknown and absent tables supply no abilities. Optional raw numeric land_dec_stake_needed is preserved when present. Source precision is preserved in existing fields; no extra requests or per-card lookups are added.
